• it seeks to understand the vital connections between plants and animals and the world around them.

• The **right to freedom of religion** is enshrined in** Articles 25-28** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 25:- **Guarantees individuals the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• **Article 26:-** Grants religious denominations the right to manage their religious affairs, including establishing religious institutions.
 
• **Article 27:-** Prohibits the state from compelling individuals to pay taxes for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
 
• **Article 28:-** Ensures that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained by the state.
 
 
 
• **Right to freedom**

• **Article 19:-** Guarantees **six freedoms **in India:
 
 
• Freedom of **speech and expression.**
 
• Freedom to **assemble peacefully and without arms**.
 
• Freedom to** form associations or unions**.
 
• Freedom to **move freely throughout India**.
 
• Freedom to **reside and settle in any part of India**.
 
• Freedom to **practice any profession, trade, or business**.
 
 
 
• **Article 20:-** Protects against double jeopardy and self-incrimination.
 
• **Article 21:-** Ensures the right to life and personal liberty.
 
• **Article 22:- **Safeguards individuals against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
 
 
• **Right to equality**
 
 
• The** right to equality** is enshrined in **Articles 14-18** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Article 14:- **Guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all individuals within the territory of India.
 
• **Article 15:- **Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16:- **Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits discrimination in employment on the same grounds as Article 15.
 
• **Article 17:-** Abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18:-** Abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.

questions.question: Why do pickles last longer?

options.text: Only beneficial bacteria can grow in the pickle.
The water content of the pickle protect the pickle from spoilage.
Pickle is prepared in a vacuum so that no harmful bacteria can grow on it.
Bacterial and fungal cells get plasmolysed in high salt concentration of pickle.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__** Bacterial and fungal cells get plasmolysed in high salt concentrations of pickle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pickles **last longer primarily because of the high salt concentration used in their preparation, which causes bacterial and fungal cells to undergo** plasmolysis,** making the environment inhospitable for their growth. 
 
• During the pickling process, beneficial bacteria (such as **lactic acid bacteria**) play a crucial role.
 
• They ferment the sugars present in the vegetables, producing **lactic acid**. 
 
• This acidic environment inhibits the growth of harmful bacteria and preserves the pickle. So, while beneficial bacteria thrive, harmful ones are suppressed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When vegetables are submerged in a brine solution (which contains salt or vinegar), the high salt concentration draws water out of the cells through **osmosis**.
 
• The **reduced water availability prevents the growth of spoilage-causing microorganisms.**
 
• While **vacuum sealing **is used for certain types of pickles, it is not a universal method. 
 
• Vacuum-sealed pickles are prepared in an **environment devoid of oxygen**, preventing the growth of aerobic bacteria and molds.
 
• However, most pickles rely on the natural fermentation process rather than vacuum sealing.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary arylamine in which an amino functional group is substituted for one of the benzene hydrogens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Aniline__* ***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Primary arylamines are derivatives of ammonia (**NH**₃) where one hydrogen atom is replaced by an aryl group (a type of aromatic hydrocarbon), directly attached to the nitrogen atom. 
 
• **Quinoline** is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that includes a benzene ring fused to a pyridine ring. It doesn't fit the definition of a primary arylamine because the amino group is not part of its structure.

 
• **Aniline** is the simplest primary arylamine, where the amino group (-NH₂) is directly bonded to a benzene ring. This matches the description provided in the question.

 
• **Pyridine** is a basic heterocyclic aromatic organic compound similar to benzene, with one methine group (=CH−) replaced by a nitrogen atom, but it does not have an amino (-NH2) group attached directly to the ring, so it isn't a primary arylamine.

 
• **Toluidines** include o-toluidine, m-toluidine, and p-toluidine, which are all methyl derivatives of aniline. Like aniline, toluidines are primary arylamines because they have an amino group directly attached to a benzene ring. However, due to the methyl group, they are not the simplest form of primary arylamine, unlike aniline.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) per unit be 100, which means Cost Price (CP) per unit = 100 − 12 = 88.

The shopkeeper's overall profit multiplier is 125 / 100 (since he earns a 25% profit).

Overall Gain Factor = Price Factor × Weight Factor

125 / 100 = (100 / 88) × (Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ)

Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ = (125 / 100) × (88 / 100) = 110 / 100 = 11 / 10

The machine shows 11 units for every 10 units of actual weight, showing 1 extra unit per 10 units. Percentage extra = (1 / 10) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) is 12% less than the Selling Price (SP).

Overall profit earned by the shopkeeper = 25%.

**Formula Used:**

Overall SP / Overall CP = (SP per unit / CP per unit) × (Shown Weight / Actual Weight)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3232e9a3b580247fe02e25959a0746e2ad0513c94158edb226547daed89afccf.png]

⇒ Let the Selling Price per unit be ₹100.

⇒ Cost Price per unit = ₹100 − 12% = ₹88.

⇒ Let the machine display Wₛₕₒwₙ units of weight, while the actual physical weight dispensed is Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ units.

⇒ Overall CP incurred by the shopkeeper = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ

⇒ Overall SP charged from the customer = 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ

⇒ Since the overall profit is 25%, we know that Overall SP = Overall CP × 1.25

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ × (125 / 100)

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ × (5 / 4)

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 110 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ

⇒ Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ = 110 / 100 = 11 / 10

⇒ This means for every 10 units of actual weight, the machine falsely shows 11 units.

⇒ Extra weight shown by the faulty machine = 11 − 10 = 1 unit.

⇒ Percentage more weight shown = (Extra Weight / Actual Weight) × 100

⇒ Percentage more weight shown = (1 / 10) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer manipulates both price and weight, the effective profit multiplier is determined by the product of the price multiplier (SP ÷ CP) and the weight multiplier (Weight Charged ÷ Actual Weight Given).

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is fundamentally evaluated on the base of the Cost Price (CP). The foundational formula is Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

For multiple distinct profit sources, the overall change can be established rapidly using multiplying factors. For instance, a 25% profit strictly translates to a multiplier factor of (100 + 25) / 100 = 125 / 100 or 5 / 4.

questions.question: Find the mean proportion of x³y and xy³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Mean Proportion** between **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Given values: **a = x³y** and **b = xy³**.

Mean Proportion = √(x³y × xy³) = √(x⁴y⁴) = **x²y²**.

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61356aee096894ad366dfec0a4437de6e3354fcea923a8b88035ca9a40fbdd04.png] 

**Given:** First term (a) = **x³y**, Last term (b) = **xy³**.

⇒ M² = x⁽³⁺¹⁾ × y⁽¹⁺³⁾

⇒ M² = x⁴y⁴

⇒ M = √(x⁴y⁴)

⇒ M = (x⁴)¹/² × (y⁴)¹/²

⇒ M = x²y²

**∴ The correct answer is x²y².**

**__Additional Information__**

Third Proportion

The **Third Proportion** of two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **c** such that **a : b = b : c**, which gives **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportion

The **Fourth Proportion** of three numbers **a, b,** and **c** is **d** such that **a : b = c : d**, which gives **d = (b × c)/a**.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios **a : b** and **c : d**, the **Compound Ratio** is **(a × c) : (b × d)**.</p

questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs. 1,200 in 2 years and becomes Rs. 1,260 in 3 years at compound interest, when interest is compounded annually. What is the rate of compound interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

 
• The amount after 2 years is Rs. 1,200.
 
• The amount after 3 years is Rs. 1,260.

Let P be the principal amount and r be the annual interest rate.

From the compound interest formula:

The amount A after t years is given by:

 A = P (1 + r)t

Using the given information:

 
• After 2 years: 1200 = P (1 + r)2
 
• After 3 years: 1260 = P (1 + r)3

To find r , divide the second equation by the first equation to eliminate P :

( (1260)/(1200) = (P (1 + r)³)/(P (1 + r)²) )

( (1260)/(1200) = 1 + r )

 

⇒1 + r = 1260/1200

⇒ 1 + r = 1.05 

⇒ r = 0.05 

So, the rate of compound interest per annum is:

⇒ r = 0.05 × 100% = 5 %

Therefore, the rate of compound interest per annum is 5 %

[SI₁ = (P1 times R times T1)/(100)]+ [SI₂ = (P2 times R times T2)/(100)]

**The rate of interest is 5% annually.**
